stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OHWZ The only known remaining photo of resistance fighter Eva Mamlok Image: Familienarchiv Siemsen Advertisement In the history of German resistance to Nazism , some names have become symbols: Sophie Scholl , Claus von Stauffenberg , Dietrich Bonhoeffer and Georg Elser . Yet many others have remained largely forgotten. Among them is Eva Mamlok, a young Jewish woman from Berlin whose acts of defiance began in her teenage years and continued until her murder in a Nazi concentration camp. Now more people will get to know her story as Berlin renames Blücherplatz, a square in the district of Kreuzberg, Eva-Mamlok-Platz on October 16. "Eva Mamlok was a very remarkable person.
